encoding.rule: Web (rowMatchesSearch, WP09 §1.2 and WAVES §4.1 item 10): q = query.trim(); an empty q is no search and every row shows. A row matches when q, compared case-insensitively (toLocaleLowerCase of both sides, no diacritic folding), is a substring of the displayed text of one field of the row. Every field whose per-view visibility is not AlwaysHidden (2) is searched, the primary field always; fields are never concatenated. Displayed text: select ids resolve to option names, numbers print as stored (no number format here), URLs as written.
encoding.desktop: Desktop keeps its Tantivy search over every visible field (a superset with token-prefix and fuzzy matching, row page text and person emails). It is not changed; parity holds on queries[].
encoding.fields: visibility is the per-view field visibility (0 AlwaysShown, 1 HideWhenEmpty, 2 AlwaysHidden); absent means AlwaysShown. options are [id, name] pairs.
encoding.rows: One object per row in creation order; a key is a field id, its value the cell: text, a number, an option id or a list of option ids. An absent key is an empty cell.
encoding.row_documents: Text on the row's page (its document), by row id. Web does not search it.
encoding.queries: Every query gives the same ids on both clients, in row order (no sorts).
encoding.known_divergences: The only queries where the engines differ: web and desktop ids in row order and why.

row_documents.r2: Kickoff notes for the zephyr pilot

known_divergences.why: desktop fuzzy matching: a word one edit away from a token (acne, acme) matches
web substring inside a word; desktop matches whole tokens and token prefixes only
desktop matches every word anywhere in the row; web needs the whole query inside one field
desktop also indexes the row page text
